findings.issue: W08ScreenshotDiff now asserts Assert.InRange(percentage, 33.30 ± 0.5) against a baseline measured on this one machine, and is kept green by a fixed `await page.WaitForTimeoutAsync(250)` that the builder added to mask a compositor-paint race in WSidebar.razor / the theme-application path (outside the package's allowed paths). Both are honest and documented in-code and in open_issues, and the review's fix text did ask for 'a tolerance around the recorded baseline' — but the combination makes the only screenshot test in the suite dependent on this display's sub-pixel font rendering and on a wall-clock guess, so it will need re-baselining on any other machine and can regress silently to flaky if the race widens.
findings.fix: No change required in this package. When B1-B8 introduce per-screen budgets, replace the symmetric InRange with an upper bound (Assert.True(percentage <= budget)) so a machine that renders closer to the export cannot fail, move the baseline/tolerance constants into one shared, clearly-named file the later packages read, and remove the 250 ms settle once WSidebar.razor / the theme-application startup path is fixed at the source (replace it with a signal the page itself raises after the themed first paint).

verify2-firstrun 3 (orphaned vault blobs) — closed and genuinely tested. ActivateAsync threads a `writtenVaultHashes` list through StoreAttachmentsAsync/StoreAsync, both RollBack call sites (DiskFull and the general rethrow) pass it, and RollBack deletes VaultStore.Delete(hash) plus VaultFilePath(hash)+".tmp" with the same swallowed IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException guard as the key-file and database deletes. VaultStore.Write additionally wraps the stream write + File.Move and deletes its own .tmp on failure. FirstRunWalkthroughTests.An_activation_that_fails_after_the_first_attachment_removes_that_attachment_too occupies the guide's vault slot with a directory so the logo lands and the guide fails, then asserts the key file, the database, the logo blob and the guide .tmp are all gone, IsActivated/AlreadyActivated false, and that the same file and sheet then activate cleanly with both blobs present. That is a real fault injection, not a tautology — remove the RollBack loop and it fails on the logo assertion. Rollback now leaves no orphaned vault blob.
verify2-firstrun 4 (recovery counter forgets history) — closed twice over: RecoverAsync clears _lastCountedCode on the Success path, and CountWrongCode clears it whenever _login.Profile().FailedAttempts == 0, which is the OpenSessionAsync reset the finding's second half asked for. A_successful_sign_in_forgets_the_last_wrong_recovery_code drives wrong code -> FailedAttempts 1 -> successful password sign-in -> FailedAttempts 0 -> the same code text again -> FailedAttempts 1. It fails without the reset.
verify2-firstrun 5 (idle lock-out) — closed: W05Login implements IDisposable, starts one ITimer at LockService.TickInterval (15 s) from both the initial standing-lock path and the SignInAsync LockedOut path, CheckLockTimer runs on the renderer thread via InvokeAsync, clears _result, stops itself and calls StateHasChanged, and Dispose stops it. FixedTime now returns a ManualTimer so both new tests are deterministic (no Thread.Sleep, no real timer): one fires the timer by hand after clearing LockedUntil and asserts the button re-enables, the danger card disappears and the timer is disposed; the other asserts DisposeComponents stops a still-running timer.
